newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese troops stream towards border with HK.
newsitem.headline: Chinese troops stream towards border with HK.

text.p: Troops of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) on Monday set off amid cheers on the first leg of their march into Hong Kong to assert Chinese sovereignty over the territory at midnight.

The first 509 soldiers, due to march into Hong Kong at 9.00 p.m. (1300 GMT), streamed out of the barracks in a cavalcade of 39 army-green trucks towards the border after a solemn departure ceremony and a speech by China's top military officer.
Some waved from open trucks to cheering crowds, who lined the road leading to the border waving red ribbons, beating drums and clashing cymbals to hail the transfer of power over Hong Kong.

Groups of army, navy and air force soldiers marched out in 48 rows of four soldiers while retired militia and young women dressed in white waved to the troops, who within hours will take over the defence of Hong Kong under the Chinese flag.
A second wave of 4,000 will stream across the border by land, sea and air just six hours after the midnight handover.

"You must love the people of Hong Kong and maintain the rights and interests of the Hong Kong people at every moment," General Liu Huaqing, vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission, told the departure ceremony for the garrison.
"You must respect Hong Kong's social system and the way of living," Liu told the soldiers, seated in neat rows on stools at the garrison headquarters near the boomtown of Shenzhen.
The entry of the PLA troops has stirred anxiety over possible military action against civilians such as Beijing's 1989 suppression of student-led democracy protesters.
However Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen assured his British counterpart Robin Cook that the new garrison would be involved only in external defence.

"With your actual deeds (you must) win the support and love of the Hong Kong people," Liu told the soldiers who will sweep into Hong Kong to seal China's resumption of sovereignty after 156 years of British colonial rule.

President Jiang Zemin, who is also head of the Communist Party and chairman of the Central Military Commission, signed a formal decree on Monday ordering the PLA garrison to take up their duties in defence of Hong Kong from midnight.
"You have to devote yourselves to maintain Hong Hong's prosperity and stability. I hope you will remember this," Liu told the troops.

"You must always remember to serve the people with all your heart," Liu said, urging the soldiers to uphold Hong Kong's mini-constitution and the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's "one country, two systems" formula under which the territory retains its capitalist way of life unchanged for 50 years.
"Do everything according to the law," Liu said.

"I hope that you can bring justice into full play to resist all kinds of evil winds and noxious influences," Liu said, apparently referring to China's fears that Western liberalism could erode puritan communist values.
Above the soldiers fluttered a huge white banner emblazoned with scarlet Chinese characters exhorting: "Safeguard the prosperity and stability of Hong Kong".

The United States has joined Britain in criticising the decision to send in 4,000 troops by armoured cars, helicopters and warships. About 200 PLA soldiers have been in the colony for weeks carrying out logistics tasks for the arrival of the main force.
